newsitem.title: UGANDA: Uganda Oct inflation edges up to 9.2 pct vs Sept.
newsitem.headline: Uganda Oct inflation edges up to 9.2 pct vs Sept.

text.p: Uganda's composite annual inflation edged up to 9.2 percent in October compared to 9.1 percent in September, the central Bank of Uganda (BoU) said on Thursday.
The central bank said in a report that the September figure had been revised up to take into account education costs. It did not say what the original forecast was.
"The inflationary pressure, which was most pronounced in September at a peak of 3.5 percent, eased in October leading to a 1.9-percent monthly change," the central bank said.

"The Uganda Importers and Exporters Traders' Association VAT (value added tax) strike which affected the prices of mostly food items in the first week of October was short-lived, but the inflationary speculations among the traders has contributed to the present inflationary pressure," it added.
It said that pressure was more pronounced in the eastern cities of Jinja and Mbale where the food, beverages, tobacco, rent, fuel and utilities indices rose remarkably.

"To combat the inflationary pressures, net treasury bill issues stepped up to 5-6 billion shillings in the weekly auction, and additional policy measures were being considered," the central bank said.

It said the treasury bill market witnessed a general increase in annualised rates. The end-October rates stood at 13.16, 14.18 and 14.57 percent for the 91-, 182- and 273-day bills, respectively, compared to 11.92, 13.26 and 14.02 percent, respectively, at the end of september.
"The rise in the annualised discount rates was a reflection of the tight monetary and fiscal policy stance," it said.

The amount offered in October was 31 billion shillings compared to 19 billion shillings in September. In line with the monetary policy objective of containing inflationary pressures during the month, net sales of treasury bills were stepped up to 7.43 billion compared to 6.72 billion in September.
